raw_response:
I've been farming this same land for thirty years and my mother farmed it before me. I know this soil. My 3.5 mu runs wheat in winter and maize in summer — same rotation I've always done, same as my neighbors. My son and daughter-in-law bring in cash from the city, so the farm doesn't have to do everything, but I still need a good harvest to cover household food and inputs.

For **wheat**, I'll plant in early October after the maize comes off. I'll hire the rotary tiller to turn the stalks in. I use the improved variety seed from the township supply station — not the old seed I saved myself, those yields dropped off years ago. I put down compound fertilizer when I plant, then urea at jointing stage. I'll irrigate before the ground freezes, once in spring when it greens up, and once at heading. That's three times total. I'll spray herbicide in spring and fungicide once if I see rust on the leaves — two applications. Harvest in mid-June.

For **maize**, I plant right after wheat harvest, usually late June. Hybrid seed — everyone uses it now, the yields are worth the cost. I do rotary tillage again to work in the wheat stubble. I split fertilizer: compound fertilizer at planting, urea at big bell stage. Summer gets some rain so I only irrigate twice if it's a normal year. I spray herbicide at emergence and watch for corn borer — one more spray if I need it.
